title: Large bf16 GEMM through cuBLAS
job: One bf16 GEMM C = A·B with M=16384, N=28672, K=8192 (a Llama-3-70B MLP up-projection over 16,384 tokens), bf16 inputs and output, fp32 accumulation, through torch.mm, which calls cuBLAS. Time per GEMM, back to back.
derivation: hbm_bytes = 2 B × (M·K + K·N + M·N) = 2 × (134,217,728 + 234,881,024 + 469,762,048) = 1.68 GB: each operand read once and C written once, the minimum traffic
launches = 1: one cuBLAS kernel per GEMM

observation.metric: median wall time per GEMM; the Timer synchronizes CUDA before reading the clock

tolerance.why: The compute rate is napkin-bench's cuBLAS GemmEx bf16 on an 8192³ GEMM, the same library and dtype on a similar-sized problem, so a matched run should agree closely. The band allows two known sources of drift: the calibration's own seven GEMM samples spread from 1.36 to 1.60 ms (±8%) because sustained clocks and power vary (#5), and a different shape can select a different cuBLAS kernel and fill the 132 SMs differently (wave quantization).

match: same GPU model (NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3) and Modal request family as profiles/h100.measured.json
same dtype (bf16 in, fp32 accumulate) and library family (cuBLAS) as the calibration
torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction = False, so reductions stay fp32 as in the calibration
excludes: clock and power throttling during a sustained run: the estimate uses one rate
wave and tile quantization of this shape
allocation and data preparation: buffers are allocated once, before timing
